doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sneaking into the Earl Theatre to hear the big bands
summary: He and friends snuck in to watch Krupa, Dorsey, Ellington, Basie, Goodman and Shaw all day, and he met Teddy Wilson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: [laughter] Its very funny. Well, you mentioned in the Philly music scene, you mentioned the Earl Theatre. I’d love to hear a little about the bands, the people who were coming trough Philly and playing at the Earl Theatre, who you heard live. And I know, I think sometimes you said you event had to sneak in, is that right? Or sneak into after- hours jam sessions?

But you were hearing a lot of live music. DeFranco:...Yep, we used to, sometimes a side door would be open to the theatre and we’d sneak in and we’d sit there and watch three and four shows all day, you know, into the evening.
Do you remember any in particular? You mentioned Tommy Dorsey when you heard Johnny Mintz.
Oh yeah, Gene Krupa, Tommy Dorsey, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, all the big bands, Benny Goodman, Artie Shaw…
Amazing. DeFranco:…they all came through and we’d devour that music. Most of the BandBusters were there watching those shows.
Did you ever hang out with any of the musicians? Or talk to them?
No, well we tried to. Occasionally we would be lucky enough to link up with some, you know, somebody from. I remember talking with Teddy Wilson for quite sometime, he was really nice.
